newsitem.title: FINLAND: AAMULEHTI CEO SEES AD REVENUE GROWTH.
newsitem.headline: AAMULEHTI CEO SEES AD REVENUE GROWTH.

text.p: Finnish media group Aamulehti-yhtyma Oy sees an upturn in advertising helping its merger with domestic broadcaster MTV Oy to a good start next year though competition will be fierce, the group's CEO said on Friday.

"The economy looks set to continue growing and, on the basis of the performance of the early part of this year, it seems that advertising revenues in all media have headed upwards," Aamulehti CEO Matti Packalen told Reuters.
The company, due to start operations in March 1996, will be called Alma Media Oyj. It intends to apply for a bourse listing.

"(Competition), of course, will have an impact on how the operations get started," Packalen said, adding: "As far as 1998 is concerned, I do not expect to see a terrribly big swing in total earnings."
"The trend (in earnings) will be fairly stable," Packalen said, but declined to elaborate.

His remarks were in response to a question on the prospects for the new company to be created next March by the merger of Aamulehti and Finnish commercial television operator MTV Oy, announced in April.
Based on 1996 financial performance, the new group would have net sales in excess of 2.6 billion markka and about 3,600 employees, Aamulehti said in its merger prospectus.

That would make it one of the biggest and most diversified media groups in the Nordic region, Aamulehti said. Sweden's Tidnings AB Marieberg , Aamulehti's biggest owner, has said it intends to own about a fifth of the new group.

In terms of revenues the new company is expected to be the leader in the Finnish media industry, leapfrogging domestic publishing rival Sanoma Corporation, which had 1996 net sales of 1.8 billion markka.
"Newspaper circulations clearly indicate growth, but the competitive situation will change next year," Packalen said.

The merged Aamulehti/MTV group will face competition in the television business from a new nationwide channel, "Nelonen," launched last weekend by a unit of the Erkko family's media empire, which publishes the leading daily Helsingin Sanomat.
Aamulehti's business newspaper Kauppalehti, which up to now has had the daily business newspaper market all to itself, will also have a new competitor next year, Packalen noted.
He was referring to the plans of Erkko's Sanoma group to expand into printed and electronic business news.
Packalen said he regarded both the new television channel and Sanoma's planned business newspaper as serious competitors backed by considerable resources.
"It's too early to say how competition in the television business will develop," he said.

But Packalen said the merged Aamulehti/MTV could lose 10 to 20 percent of its television advertising revenues to the newcomer during the next two years, but that he would be very satisfied if it retained a market share of about 80 percent.
"We believe that the total media cake -- that is, advertising revenues -- will grow by about four percent per year up to about the year 2000, and most of the growth will be in television," he said.

Revenue growth from TV commercials was expected to be about 10 percent per year, and that growth would be shared by two commercial TV operators. Earlier, MTV was Finland's only nation-wide television channel carrying commercials.
The Finnish media market was becoming so crowded that potential for really big growth existed only in acquisitions, Packalen said.
Aamulehti earlier reported January-April pre-tax profit up 59 percent to 51 million markka.
In 1996, Aamulehti had profit before extraordinary items and taxes of 155 million markka on net sales of 1.62 billion markka.
Increasingly engaged in the electronic media, Aamulehti together with MTV is part of a consortium that this year was granted a licence for nationwide commercial radio broadcasting.

Radio broadcasting would remain a sideline business for the merged group Packalen said, predicting that net sales from radio operations would be 50-100 million markka after two full years in operation.
Aamulehti's share price soared on the April merger news, and to date has risen 28 percent this year, slightly outpacing the all-share HEX index's rise of 23 percent this year.
On Friday after the release of its four-month report, Aamulehti traded 8.50 markka higher at 180.00 on the Helsinki bourse, in fair seven million markka volume.
